sourceEnglishTitle: Motivating the Crew Through a Hot Week
sourceEnglishObjective: Keep a tired crew going through a heat wave with a clear plan, firm commitments and real encouragement
sourceEnglishSpeaking: You are the crew lead and the AI is a tired crew member during a heat wave with a deadline: acknowledge the hard week, give the plan and your commitments with the future (empezaremos, habrá), and make water and breaks non-negotiable.
sourceSpanishReaderTitle: Five Hot Days and One Deadline

examples.es: Empezaremos a las seis y habrá agua fría todo el día.
examples.en: We'll start at six and there will be cold water all day.

examples.es: Vamos a terminar a tiempo, pero nadie trabajará sin descanso.
examples.en: We're going to finish on time, but nobody will work without a break.

example.target: Pararemos a las dos, antes de lo peor del calor.
example.native: We'll stop at two, before the worst of the heat.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Future for a commitment: pararemos, empezaremos.

example.target: Si te mareas, me avisas en ese momento.
example.native: If you get dizzy, tell me right away.

example.target: Si te mareas, bajas a la sombra.
example.native: If you get dizzy, you come down to the shade.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Reflexive verb: me mareo means I get dizzy.

example.target: Hace mucho calor y hacemos una pausa cada hora.
example.native: It's very hot and we take a break every hour.

example.target: En ese caso llamaremos al 911 sin esperar.
example.native: In that case we'll call 911 without waiting.

candidateObjective: 猛暑の中で疲れた作業班に、明確な計画、約束、励ましを伝える。
candidateFocus: ～まで sets the revised schedule's endpoint. ～たら gives a direct symptom-report condition; ～ので connects the early stop with the hottest hours.

archivedForms.exampleEnglish: We'll stop at two, before the worst of the heat.

archivedForms.exampleJa: めまいがしたら、すぐに教えてください。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: If you get dizzy, tell me right away.

archivedForms.exampleEnglish: If you get dizzy, you come down to the shade.

archivedForms.exampleEnglish: It's very hot and we take a break every hour.

archivedSpeaking.opening: 六時に始め、二時に終えます。毎時間、日陰で水分補給の休憩を取ります。めまいがしたらすぐに教えてください。全員で期限に間に合わせましょう。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Acknowledge a difficult heat-wave week, explain the changed hours, water and shade breaks, and use the direct terms for dizziness, heat exhaustion and heatstroke when discussing the crew's plan.

cards.reviewNote: Heat-wave threshold and locale are unspecified in the isolated card; preserve the source scene rather than infer a universal cutoff.
Heat exhaustion is a distinct clinical term; qualified Japanese/clinical review must check 熱疲労 against the lesson context.
Heatstroke is a distinct emergency term; qualified Japanese/clinical review must check 熱射病 and urgency.
Water-break interval is a scene-specific plan, not a universal schedule.
Electrolytes appear in the source plan; do not imply they replace water or an individual medical assessment.

cards.sourceSpanish: Sé que ha sido una semana dura.
cards.sourceEnglish: I know it's been a tough week.
cards.candidateJapanese: 大変な一週間だったことは分かっています。
cards.archivedJapanese: 大変な一週間だったことは分かっています。
cards.archivedEnglish: I know it's been a tough week.

cards.sourceSpanish: Empezaremos a las seis y pararemos a las dos.
cards.sourceEnglish: We'll start at six and stop at two.
cards.archivedJapanese: 六時に始め、二時に終えます。
cards.archivedEnglish: We'll start at six and stop at two.
cards.reviewNote: Six-to-two schedule depends on work conditions and locale; preserve the exact hours without universalizing.

cards.sourceSpanish: Habrá agua fría en la hielera todo el día.
cards.sourceEnglish: There will be cold water in the cooler all day.
cards.candidateJapanese: クーラーボックスには一日中冷たい水を用意します。
cards.archivedJapanese: クーラーボックスには一日中冷たい水を用意します。
cards.archivedEnglish: There will be cold water in the cooler all day.

cards.sourceEnglish: Nobody will work without a break.
cards.candidateJapanese: 休憩なしで働く人はいません。
cards.archivedJapanese: 休憩なしで働く人はいません。
cards.archivedEnglish: Nobody will work without a break.

cards.sourceSpanish: Si te mareas, me avisas en ese momento.
cards.sourceEnglish: If you get dizzy, tell me right away.
cards.archivedJapanese: めまいがしたら、すぐに教えてください。
cards.archivedEnglish: If you get dizzy, tell me right away.
cards.reviewNote: Dizziness reporting is a direct source instruction; confirm Japanese register and symptom wording.

cards.sourceSpanish: Terminaremos a tiempo, pero sin riesgos.
cards.sourceEnglish: We'll finish on time, but without risks.
cards.archivedJapanese: 期限どおりに終えますが、危険は冒しません。
cards.archivedEnglish: We'll finish on time, but without risks.
cards.reviewNote: Without risks is an absolute promise in the source; hold for qualified safety/source decision.

cards.archivedJapanese: みんな、全力で頑張りましょう！
cards.reviewNote: Give it your all could conflict with the heat-safety message; assess register and intent.
Archived 社長 narrows sir/boss to company president; source does not establish that title.

reader.sourceSpanish: El pronóstico anunció una ola de calor para toda la semana, con más de 100 grados por la tarde.
reader.sourceEnglish: The forecast announced a heat wave for the whole week, with more than 100 degrees in the afternoon.
reader.archivedJapanese: 予報では一週間の熱波が伝えられ、午後は華氏100度を超える見込みです。
reader.archivedEnglish: The forecast announced a heat wave for the whole week, with more than 100 degrees in the afternoon.
reader.reviewNote: The source says over 100 degrees without naming a scale; archive adds Fahrenheit. Resolve locale/temperature unit before selection.

reader.sourceSpanish: La compañía tenía una fecha límite: el techo de la escuela tenía que estar listo el viernes.
reader.sourceEnglish: The company had a deadline: the school roof had to be ready by Friday.
reader.candidateJapanese: 会社には期限があり、学校の屋根を金曜日までに仕上げる必要がありました。
reader.archivedJapanese: 会社には期限があり、学校の屋根を金曜日までに仕上げる必要がありました。
reader.archivedEnglish: The company had a deadline: the school roof had to be ready by Friday.

reader.sourceSpanish: El miércoles, en la madrugada, Rogelio reunió a la cuadrilla antes de subir.
reader.sourceEnglish: On Wednesday, in the early morning, Rogelio gathered the crew before going up.
reader.candidateJapanese: 水曜日の早朝、ロヘリオは屋根に上がる前に作業班を集めました。
reader.archivedJapanese: 水曜日の早朝、ロヘリオは屋根に上がる前に作業班を集めました。
reader.archivedEnglish: On Wednesday, in the early morning, Rogelio gathered the crew before going up.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Sé que ha sido una semana dura, y todavía faltan tres días.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: I know it's been a tough week, and there are still three days to go.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「大変な一週間だったことは分かっています。あと三日あります。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「大変な一週間だったことは分かっています。あと三日あります。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: I know it's been a tough week, and there are still three days to go.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Este es el plan: cambiaremos el horario hasta el viernes.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Here's the plan: we'll change the schedule until Friday.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「計画はこうです。金曜日まで作業予定を変えます。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「計画はこうです。金曜日まで作業予定を変えます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Here's the plan: we'll change the schedule until Friday.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Empezaremos a las seis y pararemos a las dos, antes de lo peor del calor.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: We'll start at six and stop at two, before the worst of the heat.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「六時に始め、二時に終えます。一番暑い時間の前に終わります。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: We'll start at six and stop at two, before the worst of the heat.
reader.reviewNote: The six-to-two schedule is a source commitment in this scene, not universal heat-safety timing.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Habrá agua fría en la hielera todo el día, y también electrolitos.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: There will be cold water in the cooler all day, and electrolytes too.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「クーラーボックスには一日中冷たい水と電解質を用意します。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: There will be cold water in the cooler all day, and electrolytes too.
reader.reviewNote: Cold water and electrolytes are source commitments; assess precise Japanese meaning and avoid substituting one for the other.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Cada hora haremos una pausa para tomar agua en la sombra, y nadie trabajará sin descanso.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Every hour we'll take a water break in the shade, and nobody will work without a break.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「毎時間、日陰で水分補給の休憩を取ります。休憩なしで働く人はいません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Every hour we'll take a water break in the shade, and nobody will work without a break.
reader.reviewNote: Hourly shade/water break is the source plan, not a universal rule.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: La hidratación no es opcional, aunque estemos atrasados.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Hydration isn't optional, even if we're behind.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「遅れていても、水分補給は必須です。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Hydration isn't optional, even if we're behind.
reader.reviewNote: Hydration is not optional in the source, but do not convert this scene into generic clinical advice.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Y tú, Kevin, que eres nuevo: si te mareas, me avisas en ese momento.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: And you, Kevin, since you're new: if you get dizzy, tell me right away.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「新人のケビン、めまいがしたらすぐに教えてください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: And you, Kevin, since you're new: if you get dizzy, tell me right away.
reader.reviewNote: Dizziness instruction to new hire Kevin requires precise symptom and reporting language.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: El mareo, el dolor de cabeza, la náusea y el sudor excesivo son señales de agotamiento por calor.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Dizziness, headache, nausea and heavy sweating are signs of heat exhaustion.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「めまい、頭痛、吐き気、大量の発汗は熱疲労の兆候です。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Dizziness, headache, nausea and heavy sweating are signs of heat exhaustion.
reader.reviewNote: The source lists dizziness, headache, nausea and heavy sweating as heat-exhaustion signs; qualified clinical/Japanese review is required.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Un golpe de calor es una emergencia, y en ese caso llamaremos al 911 sin esperar.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Heatstroke is an emergency, and in that case we'll call 911 without waiting.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「熱射病は緊急事態です。その場合は待たずに911へ電話します。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Heatstroke is an emergency, and in that case we'll call 911 without waiting.
reader.reviewNote: Heatstroke is named as an emergency with 911 in the source; confirm site locale and Japanese clinical term before scored use.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Terminaremos a tiempo, pero sin riesgos; el esfuerzo de cada uno cuenta.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: We'll finish on time, but without risks; everyone's effort counts.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「期限どおりに終えますが、危険は冒しません。全員の努力が大切です。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: We'll finish on time, but without risks; everyone's effort counts.
reader.reviewNote: Without risks and on-time finish are absolute promises; preserve source meaning while flagging safety/claim review.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Y el viernes, al final de la jornada, habrá tacos para todos.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: And on Friday, at the end of the workday, there will be tacos for everyone.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「金曜日の作業終わりには、全員にタコスを用意します。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「金曜日の作業終わりには、全員にタコスを用意します。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: And on Friday, at the end of the workday, there will be tacos for everyone.

reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Give it your all, guys!
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「みんな、全力で頑張りましょう！」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Give it your all, guys!
reader.reviewNote: Give it your all may counter the earlier heat-rest instruction; resolve tone in context.

reader.sourceSpanish: Por la tarde, Rogelio llamó al jefe: Cuente con nosotros, señor; el viernes estará listo.
reader.sourceEnglish: In the afternoon, Rogelio called the boss: Count on us, sir; it will be ready on Friday.
reader.archivedJapanese: 午後、ロヘリオは上司に電話し、「お任せください。金曜日に仕上がります」と伝えました。
reader.archivedEnglish: In the afternoon, Rogelio called the boss: Count on us, sir; it will be ready on Friday.
reader.reviewNote: The Friday completion assurance is a source claim, not guaranteed by the revised schedule.

write.label: Write the schedule, hourly break plan, and source emergency number.

curriculumAdaptationNote: The source presents a heat-wave week at a school roof, a six-to-two revised schedule, water/electrolytes and hourly shade breaks, symptom reporting, heatstroke emergency language and a Friday deadline. The source says more than 100 degrees but does not identify the scale; archived Japanese adds Fahrenheit. Hold clinical terminology, emergency number locale, break/schedule claims and absolute no-risk/on-time promises for qualified source, Japanese and domain review. The lesson must teach heat exhaustion and heatstroke directly, without erasing either term. Grammar and five Spanish verbs are pinned separately. No selected learner/audio text or progress identity is created.
